title: Apostles’ and Peter’s hymns: ‘loose us by command’; Peter binds and opens heaven by word
source_text: LIX. Sic in hymno qui incipit Exultet caelum laudibus, ad Apostolos dicitur, Qui caelum verbo clauditis, Serasque ejus solvistis, Nos a peccatis omnibus, Solvite jussi, quaesumus. Quorum praecepto subditur Salus & languor omnium, Sanate egros moribus, Nos reddentes virtutibus. Quibus consona sunt illa quae in Breviario ad Apostolos eosdem dici solent, Qui templa caeli clauditis, Serasque verbo solvitis, Nos a reatu noxio, Solvi jubete, quaesumus. Praecepta quorum protinus, Languor salusque sentiunt, Sanate mentes languidas, Augete nos virtutibus. Ad Petrum vero speciatim concipitur haec precatio: Jam bone Pastor Petre, clemens accipe Vota precantum, & peccati vincula Resolve tibi potestate tradita, Qua cunctis caelum verbo claudis, aperis. Quo pertinet etiam illud ad Joannem Baptistam: Nunc potens nostri meritis opem Pectoris duros lapides, repelle, Asperum planans iter & reflexos Dirige calles, Ubi Sanctus ille rogatur, ut ista nobis praestet, tanquam potens nostri per merita sua effectus.
pass_a_gloss: Thus in the hymn which begins Exultet caelum laudibus it is said to the Apostles: You who shut heaven by a word and have loosed its bars, Loose us from all sins, commanded, we ask. To whose precept is added Health and sickness of all, Heal the sick in morals, Restoring us with virtues. Consonant with which are those things which in the Breviary are accustomed to be said to the same Apostles: You who shut the temples of heaven and loose the bars by a word, Bid us be loosed from harmful guilt, we ask. Whose precepts at once sickness and health feel; Heal languid minds, Increase us with virtues. But to Peter specially this prayer is conceived: Now good Shepherd Peter, graciously receive the vows of those praying, and loose the bonds of sin by the power handed over to thee, by which thou shuttest and openest heaven to all by a word. To which also pertains that to John the Baptist: Now powerful, by merits grant help to us; drive back the hard stones of the breast, leveling the rough way and directing bent paths—where that Saint is asked to furnish those things to us as powerful of our effect through his merits.
pass_b_english: Apostles’ hymn: shut/open heaven by word; loose sins ‘by command.’
Peter is asked to loose sin-bonds by the power given him; the Baptist to clear the heart’s hard stones by his merits.
